Key dates

  • In-person early voting: October 20, 2026 to October 30, 2026. Early voting starts statewide on October 20. Days, hours and locations are set by each county, so check with your county clerk.
  • Voter registration deadline (county clerk must receive it by 5 p.m.): October 23, 2026. Missed the deadline? You can still register in person at an early voting site or on Election Day if you bring two forms of ID.
  • Last day to request a mail ballot (5 p.m.): October 27, 2026. Active registered voters get a ballot in the mail automatically. Your county clerk must receive your mail ballot by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or you can put it in a drop box by then.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Mountain Time.

Official election information: vote.gov

Ballot measures

Constitutional Amendment A

This amendment changes how proposed constitutional amendments are published. Instead of being printed in newspapers, they would be published for the 60 days right before the general election in a way set by state law.

Yes: A FOR vote removes the newspaper publication requirement from the constitution. State law would then have the Lieutenant Governor post the full text of proposed amendments and other ballot questions from the Legislature on the Utah Public Notice Website and the Lieutenant Governor's website for the 60 days before the general election.
No: An AGAINST vote keeps the constitution's current requirement that proposed constitutional amendments be published in newspapers before the election.

Constitutional Amendment B

This amendment would require citizen-proposed laws (initiatives) that raise taxes compared to current law to win at least 60% of the vote, instead of a simple majority.

Yes: A FOR vote means a citizen initiative voted on after November 1, 2026 that creates a new tax, expands or raises an existing tax, or makes a property tax rate go down less than it would under current law would need at least 60% voter approval to pass.
No: An AGAINST vote keeps the current rule: a citizen initiative passes with a simple majority of the votes cast on it, including initiatives that raise taxes.
